extracted.intended_audience: applicants, producers, representatives, and national IP offices involved in registration and enforcement of trade names, geographical indications, and copyright within Member States of the Organization
extracted.subtask_short: GI and trade name registration rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/substantive standards for filing, examining, registering, publishing, opposing, renewing, restoring, transferring and enforcing trade names and geographical indications, plus related definitions for copyright. Covers required documents, timings, rights conferred, penalties, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical errors in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraphs, the Organization may correct obvious clerical errors contained in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies both to trade name and geographical indication applications (similar provision repeated for GI). Organization may itself correct obvious material defects (see Article 14(6) for GIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of rejection to High Commission of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the date of notification of the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Commission of Appeal. The decision of the High Commission of Appeal shall not be appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified for trade name and geographical indication rejections and restoration rejections (time limit and finality emphasized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of registration contents (trade name)
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of the registration, the owner shall be furnished with a certificate containing: (a) the registration number of the trade name; (b) the filing date and filing number of the application and the date of registration; (c) the trade name as registered; (d) the location of the commercial establishment and the type of activity; (e) the surname, first name and address of the owner of the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate must include these particulars; Organization publishes the same information (Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of registered trade name information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each registered trade name, the Organization shall publish the information stipulated in Article 11 together with the name and address of the agent, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication uses format laid down by implementing regulations (see other Articles for publication of invalidity/restoration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of trade name registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration of a trade name shall be valid for only 10 years from the date of filing; the right may be preserved indefinitely through successive renewals every 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewals obtained by application during final year and payment of renewal fee fixed by regulation; six-month grace period after expiry with surcharge payable (Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal procedure and fees (trade name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal may be obtained on application by the owner, submitted during the final year of the 10-year period and on payment of a renewal fee whose amount shall be fixed by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner has six-month grace period after expiry to make valid payment and must pay a surcharge (Article 13(2)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed trade name registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where protection has not been renewed owing to circumstances beyond the control of the owner, the owner or entitled persons may apply for restoration on payment of the requisite renewal fee and of a surcharge, within six months of the date on which the circumstances ceased to exist, and no later than two years after the date on which renewal was due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include documents proving payment and a statement of grounds; restoration does not extend the maximum duration; restored trade names are published; rejection appealable within 60 days (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation of trade name
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a registered trade name may at any time renounce the trade name by a written declaration sent to the Organization. The renunciation shall take effect on the date on which it is entered in the special register of trade names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple written declaration suffices; entry in special register determines effective date (Article 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity of trade name registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic courts shall declare invalidation of effects of registration on application by the Office of the Public Prosecutor or any interested natural or legal person. The court shall declare registration invalid if it is not consistent with Articles 1, 2 and 5(1) or conflicts with a prior right; in event of such conflict, invalidity may only be declared on application by the owner of the prior right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decision becomes final it shall be notified to the Organization and entered in the special register; invalidity shall be published in implementing regulations' format and deemed invalid as of the date on which it occurs (Article 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and assignment of trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name may be assigned or transferred only with the trade, industrial, craft or agricultural establishment, or with the part of such establishment designated under the trade name. Assignment shall be in writing and require signatures of contracting parties; transfers by merger or succession may be proved by other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts are enforceable against third parties only if entered in the special register and published in prescribed format; Organization keeps a copy (Article 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal remedies and penalties for trade name infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where rights attaching to a trade name are threatened with infringement, the owner may initiate legal action to prevent such infringement. On infringement, the owner may prohibit continuation and request damages and other civil penalties. Criminal penalties apply for affixing or altering names or trade names falsely: imprisonment 3 months to 1 year and fine 5,000,000 to 15,000,000 CFA francs, or one of these penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court determines damages taking into account adverse financial effects, profits made by perpetrator and moral damage; knowingly displaying falsified names liable to same punishment (Article 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of applicability for trade name provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Annex shall be applicable to any trade, industrial, craft or agricultural establishment, subject to special provisions applicable elsewhere to such establishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies general applicability (Article 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued validity of prior Bangui trade name registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any trade name registered or recognized under the Bangui Agreement, Act of February 24, 1999 and its Annex V shall remain in force for the term specified in that Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional protection for pre-existing registrations (Article 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquired rights and transitional application (trade names)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Annex applies to trade name applications made as from the day of its entry into force, subject to rights acquired under Annex V of the Bangui Agreement. Applications filed prior to entry remain subject to provisions applicable on their filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects acquired rights while applying new rules to applications filed after entry into force (Article 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "geographical indication"
rubrics_metrics.description: "geographical indication" means an indication that serves to identify a product as originating from a place, a region, or a country, in those cases where the quality, reputation or other specific characteristic of the product may be essentially attributed to such geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets core substantive test for GI protection: link between product quality/reputation/characteristics and geographical origin (Annex VI Art.1(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Products and producers definitions for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: "product" means any natural, agricultural, craft or industrial product; "producer" includes farmers; manufacturers of craft or industry products; processors of natural or agricultural products; and any person who trades such products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definitions determine who may be entitled to rights and what goods are covered (Annex VI Art.1(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trans-border geographical indications allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication may concern two or more States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables GIs spanning multiple Member States (Annex VI Art.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal/invalidation of marks containing or imitating a geographical indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration of a trademark containing or imitating a geographical indication shall be refused or invalidated if the use of the indication in the trademark for such products is likely to mislead the public as to the true place of origin. Likewise, registration of a GI which, although literally accurate, suggests products originate from a different territory shall be refused or invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on likelihood of misleading public about origin (Annex VI Art.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions governing protection of GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indications shall be protected as such if they have been registered by the Organization, or are to be treated as having been registered by virtue of an international convention to which Member States or Organization are party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration by Organization or effect via international treaty are bases for protection (Annex VI Art.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: GIs excluded from protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Not protected: (a) indications not corresponding to definition in Article 1(a); (b) indications contrary to public policy or morality or likely to deceive the public as to nature, source, manufacturing process, characteristic qualities or suitability; (c) indications not protected in their country of origin or that have ceased to be protected there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets substantive exclusions including deception, public policy, and origin-country protection requirement (Annex VI Art.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by GI registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration confers on producers performing activities in the geographical area the right to use for commercial purposes the registered GI for the products listed in the register, provided such products possess the essential characteristics recorded in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where products have been put into circulation under the registered GI any person may use the GI for those products; otherwise use is illegal even if true origin stated or accompanied by qualifiers like "imitation" (Annex VI Art.6(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misleading designations and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be illegal to use in the designation or presentation of a product any device that indicates or suggests that the product originates from a geographical region other than the actual place of origin, in a manner that misleads the public as to geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers devices and presentations beyond literal names (Annex VI Art.6(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior mark coexistence exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a prior identical or similar mark to a geographical indication may continue to use his mark, save where the mark concerns agricultural, natural or craft products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides grandfathering for prior marks except for certain product categories (Annex VI Art.6(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to file for GI registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal persons operating as producers in the geographical region, groups of such persons and any competent authority shall be entitled to file an application. Exceptionally a natural person may file under conditions fixed by implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who may be applicant(s) for GIs and that regulations may allow limited exceptions (Annex VI Art.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents for GI application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file shall contain: (a) an application addressed to the Director-General; (b) proof of payment of filing fee; (c) the geographical indication; (d) a reasoned notice of validation by the competent Ministry of the State of origin; (e) the specifications including applicant, producer name, type of product, product specifications (quality, reputation, characteristics), delimitation of area, breeding method, link to origin, inspection plan, labelling; (f) articles of association of group if applicable; (g) agent’s power of attorney if applicable; (h) proof of registration of the GI in the country of origin for foreign GIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications must set out essential characteristics and control measures (Annex VI Art.8(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing rules for trans-border GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a trans-border GI concerns Member States: (a) each State may file its application; (b) all States may file a joint application. If third-party Lisbon States involved, common application pursuant to Lisbon Agreement possible. In these cases, application must contain authorization issued by competent Ministry in each State concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures proper authorizations accompany multi-state filings (Annex VI Art.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report of filing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A report prepared by the Organization or Ministry shall note each filing and specify date and time; a copy issued to the applicant; the Ministry shall transmit documents to the Organization within five working days of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes official evidence of filing and timelines for transmission (Annex VI Art.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of GI application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization shall publish for each application: application number, filing date, reproduction of the GI, name and type of product, name/address of applicant, beneficiary producer groups, geographical origin, delimitation of area, name/address of agent if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice enables opposition and transparency (Annex VI Art.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to GI registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may oppose registration within three months of publication by sending a written statement setting out reasons based on infringement of Articles 1,3,5 and 7 or a prior registered right. Applicant may reply within three months (renewable once). Organization may hear parties on request. Organization’s ruling appealable to High Commission within 60 days. If opposition well-founded, Organization shall reject application; final forfeiture ruling published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies grounds, timelines, right to be heard, appeal route and publication of final decisions (Annex VI Art.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment scope and timing for GI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be amended: (a) until ruling on registration; (b) during opposition proceedings; (c) during appellate proceedings. Amendments may only concern beneficiaries and delimitation of the geographical area. Amended application retains original filing date. Fee payable for any amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow scope of permissible amendments to prevent substantive changes after filing (Annex VI Art.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria for GI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization shall examine whether the applicant is entitled to apply, whether application contains required particulars under Articles 8 and 9, and whether prescribed fees have been paid. Lack of status or unpaid fees -> rejection. If application lacks required particulars (except sub-paragraph 2(b)) it shall be deemed irregular and applicant invited to regularize within three months (extendable 30 days); regularized application retains original filing date; failing regularization -> rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No filing may be rejected under paragraph (3) unless applicant afforded opportunity to correct; Organization may correct obvious material defects itself; appeals allowed within 60 days (Annex VI Art.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: GI registration certificate contents
rubrics_metrics.description: On registration a certificate shall be issued containing: registration number, filing number, filing date, a reproduction of the GI, name and address of owner, beneficiary producers if applicable, status of the owner, area of production, and products to which the GI applies. Organization shall attach copy of the specifications bearing the registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate provides authoritative record; Organization will publish the information and an excerpt of specifications (Annex VI Art.15-16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of GI registration and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For each certificate issued Organization shall publish the information in Article 15 together with name and address of agent if applicable; Organization shall also publish an excerpt of the specifications for each registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations fix procedures of publication (Annex VI Art.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to compliance with the specifications, the protection conferred on a geographical indication shall be of unlimited duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection is perpetual so long as specifications are complied with (Annex VI Art.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information in special register
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication of the application or registration any person may, on written application and submission of the requisite fee, obtain information, excerpts or copies of the entry in the special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public access to registry contents for transparency and enforcement (Annex VI Art.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of GI registration — inadmissible dilution
rubrics_metrics.description: Modification may concern specification, restriction or extension of the GI or producers. Any amendment resulting in a dilution of the link between the product and its region of origin shall be inadmissible. Application for amendment must describe amendments and reasons and consist of deletions or additions to the specifications; file must include application, amended specifications, and proof of payment of amendment fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects integrity of origin link; procedural requirements and fees apply (Annex VI Art.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and quality control for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control of products offered for sale or exploited under a registered GI and the prohibition from using the GI shall be determined by regulations issued by the Ministry responsible in the Member State concerned. Regulations shall fix procedures for inspection of the use of the logos of protected GIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member State regulations implement monitoring and enforcement mechanisms (Annex VI Art.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity and amendment by domestic courts for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or the Ministry may request competent domestic court to order cancellation of the registration on grounds under Article 5, or amendment where the registered geographic region does not correspond or specifications are defective or unjustified, or amendment of specifications. Notice of the application shall be given to the applicant and communicated by publication to all persons entitled to use the GI. Persons may request to intervene within time limit fixed by court. When decision finding nullity becomes final it shall be communicated to the Organization, entered in the special registry and published; invalidity takes effect from date of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-based remedies and notification/publication obligations to protect third-party rights (Annex VI Art.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil remedies against unlawful use of GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person or group of producers or consumers may bring action to end unlawful use or prohibit imminent use and to destroy labels and other documents contributing to such unlawful use. Injured party may require compensation. In determining damages, court shall consider adverse financial effects, profits of counterfeiter and moral damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows broad civil standing and remedies tailored to compensate and prevent further misuse (Annex VI Art.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal sanctions for intentional unlawful use of GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person intentionally making unlawful use of a registered GI shall be punishable by imprisonment of three months at least and one year at most and by a fine ranging from 5,000,000 to 30,000,000 CFA francs, or one only of these penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides criminal deterrence for intentional misuse (Annex VI Art.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravated penalties for recidivism and abuse of position
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties in Article 23 shall be doubled where: (a) recidivism; (b) defendant is member of the group representing the GI; (c) defendant is an employee of such group. Recidivism occurs where offender has been convicted of one of the offenses within the five previous years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increases penalties where abuse of trust or repeated offenses occur (Annex VI Art.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions for GIs and acquired rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Annex applies to applications filed from entry into force, subject to rights acquired under Annex VI of Bangui Agreement (1999). Applications filed prior to entry remain subject to prior provisions. Exercise of rights deriving from appellations of origin registered under prior provisions shall be subject to this Annex from entry into force subject to acquired rights. Annex VI of Bangui Agreement 1999 is repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manages transition from prior regime to new Annex (Annex VI Art.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of copyright terms (work, audiovisual work, applied art, joint authorship, collective/composite/photographic work, author, producer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive definitions: e.g., 'work' any literary or artistic creation; 'audiovisual work' series of related images giving impression of movement; 'work of applied art' two- or three-dimensional artistic creation with utilitarian function; 'author' natural person who created a work; 'producer' natural or legal person who takes initiative and responsibility for creating the work, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitional rules determine subject matter and rights under the copyright part of the Annex (Annex VII Part I CH1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of modes of communication and copies (broadcasting, rebroadcasting, communication to the public, public performance, reproduction, reprographic reproduction, copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms defined to cover modern and traditional modes: 'broadcasting' includes satellite and encrypted signals under certain conditions; 'communication to the public' includes making accessible by means other than distribution of copies; 'reproduction' defined broadly to include printing, engraving, mechanical, cinematographic, magnetic recording, etc.; 'reprographic reproduction' includes photocopying, digitization and storage in information systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These precise definitions govern the scope of exclusive rights and exceptions (Annex VII CH1 definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of copyright protection (nationality/publication/architecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions apply to works whose author or other original holder is a national or has habitual residence/headquarters in a Member State; works first published in a Member State or first published abroad and also published in a Member State within 30 days; works of architecture erected in a Member State. In joint authorship, suffices that one author meets nationality/residence requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also notes applicability of Agreement Revising the Bangui Agreement and that international treaties remain unaffected (Annex VII Art.2).
